title: Extending genome-wide association studies to admixed cohorts with high degrees of relatedness.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Zenodo API for both records: 10.5281/zenodo.19600120 (GWAS, genome-wide association study, summary statistics, CC-BY-4.0) holds UKBB.zip 8.9 GB, YalePenn.zip 2.3 GB, MCPS.zip 0.53 GB; 10.5281/zenodo.19576963 is 0.8 MB of analysis code. Read the zip central directories by ranged GET: MCPS has 4 gzipped per-SNP result files (GMMAT, plus Tractor-Mix joint/EUR/AMR for BMI, 115-145 MB each); YalePenn has 4 tar files (1.5-2.2 GB each) of alcohol-use-disorder score results. Did not decompress any row.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Abstract only (full text returned HTTP 500): individual-level genotypes come from UK Biobank, Yale-Penn and Mexico City Prospective Study, all of which need an access application. Only a dozen lead variants (rs IDs text-mined by Europe PMC) are named as findings.

a1_downloadable.note: Summary statistics are open on Zenodo (checked), but the individual-level genotypes and phenotypes (UK Biobank, Yale-Penn via dbGaP, MCPS) need access applications; anything beyond per-SNP summaries is controlled access.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: No natural prediction target. The files hold per-SNP betas and p-values (from the zip listing); a label such as 'ancestry-specific effect' would have to be built by contrasting EUR and AMR betas and thresholding a heterogeneity test.

a3_inputs_present.note: Summary files are keyed by variant position/ID only; any features (functional annotations, sequence) would need to be joined from external resources.

a4_units_stated.note: Betas are on trait scale per allele copy by construction; README files exist in the YalePenn folders (seen in listing, not opened).

a5_enough_rows.note: Millions of SNP rows, but the informative unit is the significant locus: the paper names roughly a dozen lead variants, far below 400 positives. Row count not verified.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~11.8 GB compressed across three zips; smallest file 115 MB gzipped
a6_fits_laptop.note: Each zip exceeds the 50 MB download cap; MCPS alone (0.53 GB) would be workable by streaming, but the full set is well over 5 GB.

a8_label_provenance.note: Any label would be a statistical estimate (mixed-model GWAS beta/p-value from Tractor-Mix or GMMAT), i.e. another model's output, not a direct measurement.

existing_models.name: Tractor (Nature Genetics 2021), the predecessor local-ancestry GWAS method
existing_models.score_and_split: Statistical method evaluated on simulations and UK Biobank admixed samples; not an ML predictor.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Assumed unrelated samples, which this paper's Tractor-Mix addresses.

existing_models.name: SDPR_admix (AJHG 2025), polygenic score method for admixed individuals
existing_models.score_and_split: Search snippet reports ~5-fold accuracy gain on All of Us versus training on PAGE; split not checked.

backbone.name: none suitable (summary statistics, not sequences or cells)

honest_claim_h3: Not applicable: this is a statistical-genetics method paper whose open output is GWAS summary statistics with only a handful of significant loci.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use variant annotations to predict which genetic variants have effects that differ between European and Native American ancestry segments.
plain_idea.train_on: Per-variant summary results from admixed Mexican, UK and US cohorts; number of informative examples (significant loci) is about a dozen, total rows unknown.
plain_idea.predict: Whether a variant's estimated effect differs by ancestry, derived from the paper's own mixed-model association estimates rather than a direct measurement.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Would help statistical geneticists prioritise ancestry-specific variants, but too few confirmed examples exist here to train or test anything.

more_or_better_data.why: Open data are summary statistics only; individual-level data sit behind UK Biobank, dbGaP and MCPS applications.

confidence_score.why: No replicate measurements; standard errors are already reported by the GWAS models themselves.

models_beatable.why: Tractor-Mix (2026) is a well-calibrated statistical method, not an ML model one would 'beat' with a learned predictor.

guaranteed_improvement.why: No joinable new data measures the same quantity the same way; the cohort data are controlled access.

ml_idea: Classify variants as ancestry-shared versus ancestry-enriched from functional annotations, using Tractor-Mix EUR/AMR betas as labels. Rejected: labels are model estimates, only ~a dozen significant loci, and raw data are controlled access.

effort.compute_note: Sizes taken from the Zenodo API and zip central directories; nothing timed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count genome-wide significant loci with heterogeneous EUR vs AMR effects in the MCPS files; the paper names only about a dozen lead variants.

verdict_reason: GWAS methods paper: open data are 11.8 GB of per-SNP summary statistics with no natural label, labels would be model estimates with ~a dozen significant loci, and individual-level cohorts are controlled access (fails A1, A2, A5, A8).
